rows.name: Chat UI to delegate coding tasks
rows.offer: A chat interface and API where developers describe work and a self-hosted agent picks a template, provisions a workspace and does the task.

flisk.reason: Flisk is the local runtime a coding agent works against, not a hosted chat product that provisions workspaces for people.

rows.name: Agent loop in the control plane
rows.offer: The agent loop runs inside the Coder server, so workspaces hold no LLM keys and need no agent software installed.

flisk.reason: There is no server-side control plane in a laptop-first runtime; the developer's own agent already runs next to Flisk.

rows.name: Sub-agent delegation with own context
rows.offer: A root agent can spawn child agents that each get their own context window and work on independent tasks in parallel.

flisk.reason: Sub-agent orchestration belongs to the coding agent itself; Flisk only runs the services those agents call.

rows.name: Conversation survives workspace rebuild
rows.offer: Chat history lives in the server database, so stopping, deleting or rebuilding a workspace does not lose the conversation.

flisk.reason: Flisk's agent resource keeps session checkpoints on a named volume that survives flisk down, but it does not store a coding agent's own chat history.

rows.name: Virtual desktop for agent computer use
rows.offer: An experimental option that gives agents a graphical desktop in the workspace to drive with screenshots, mouse and keyboard.

flisk.reason: A remote GUI desktop inside a cloud workspace has no counterpart in a local service runtime.

rows.name: Workspace skills and instruction discovery
rows.offer: The workspace agent scans for AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, skills and .mcp.json and gives chats a pinned snapshot of them.

flisk.reason: Flisk publishes portable skills and an AGENTS.md for coding agents to read, but it does not scan a project and push a context snapshot to a running agent.

rows.name: Admin-registered MCP servers for agents
rows.offer: Organization admins register external MCP servers whose tools are injected into or offered to agent chats under an availability policy.

flisk.reason: Flisk runs MCP servers as a first-class resource type routed over Streamable HTTP, but has no admin-managed registry that decides which agents may use which server.

text.contains: Standard Model Context Protocol servers over Streamable HTTP

rows.name: Cloud agents run in own workspaces
rows.offer: Agent Relay lets a vendor's cloud agent sessions execute their tool calls inside workspaces on your own Coder deployment.

flisk.reason: It bridges hosted agent vendors to remote workspaces; Flisk runs on the developer's machine and has no hosted session to relay.

rows.name: Capture prompts, tokens and tool calls
rows.offer: A gateway between coding agents and model providers records prompts, token usage, reasoning and every tool call, with Prometheus metrics and a sample Grafana dashboard.

flisk.reason: A local record of what each agent resource sent to its model and how many tokens it used would suit people building multi-agent systems on Flisk.

rows.acceptance: flisk logs or a new MCP tool in cli/src/mcp/tools.ts returns per-agent-resource LLM request and token counts; the proof is a file under docs/agents or a tool name in tools.ts.

ice.basis: Impact: agent-system builders often ask where tokens go, but Flisk users bring their own model clients. Confidence: Coder's feature is for org-wide governance, so the local mapping is a judgment. Ease: needs a capturing proxy or SDK hook beyond cli/src/commands/logs.ts.

rows.name: Per-user AI session audit trail
rows.offer: The gateway groups intercepted requests into sessions and threads and attributes each action to an authenticated user for auditors.

flisk.reason: Attribution to authenticated org users is an administrator need; a local stack has one developer.

rows.name: Group and user AI spend budgets
rows.offer: Premium admins cap AI spend per group or user over a monthly period and surface the resulting spend to users.

flisk.reason: Org-wide budgets and billing controls need a central server and identity, which Flisk does not have.

rows.name: Domain allowlist for agent processes
rows.offer: A process-level firewall limits which domains and HTTP verbs an AI agent can reach and logs blocked requests.

flisk.reason: Restricting which hosts an agent resource container can call would help people running untrusted or autonomous agents locally.

rows.acceptance: A service.json field or doctor/config verify check for an agent resource's allowed egress domains, proven by a docs page plus a text match in the generated Compose network config.

ice.basis: Impact: matters to agent-stack users who run autonomous code, but most local loops do not restrict egress. Confidence: the Coder tool is Linux jail based, so the container-level mapping is uncertain. Ease: needs egress proxy or network policy in runtime/engine/topologies/platform/net, which has none today.

rows.name: Separate sandbox for the agent
rows.offer: A template runs the AI agent in its own pod with a network policy so its file and network access differ from the user's.

flisk.reason: It is built on Kubernetes pods and network policies, and Flisk deliberately does not target Kubernetes.

rows.name: System-level process logging
rows.offer: A Premium sidecar logs every process started inside a Kubernetes workspace for security review.

flisk.reason: Linux-on-Kubernetes auditing for administrators does not fit a laptop runtime.

rows.name: Audit logs of admin and user actions
rows.offer: The server records who did what across the deployment, such as workspace and template changes, for review.

flisk.reason: There is no multi-user control plane in Flisk to audit.

rows.name: SSO, groups and access control
rows.offer: Coder supports OIDC and GitHub sign-in with MFA and groups that control who can use templates.

flisk.reason: Flisk runs as the developer's own user with no accounts, so identity and RBAC do not apply.

rows.name: Terraform workspace templates
rows.offer: Administrators define the infrastructure of every workspace as Terraform templates, with parameters and a template builder.

flisk.reason: Provisioning cloud infrastructure is the job of Coder's control plane; Flisk generates local Compose and Tilt files instead.

rows.name: Pool of prebuilt workspaces
rows.offer: The server keeps a pool of ready workspaces per parameter preset and hands one to a developer who asks, cutting wait time.

flisk.reason: Pre-provisioning cloud machines to hide creation time is not a local-runtime problem.

rows.name: Run devcontainer.json environments
rows.offer: Workspaces build and run dev containers from devcontainer.json using the Dev Containers CLI and Docker, each shown as a sub-agent.

flisk.reason: Flisk runs inside a Dev Container with Docker-outside-of-Docker, but it does not build or manage environments from devcontainer.json.

rows.name: Autostop idle workspaces
rows.offer: Workspaces can start and stop on a schedule and stop after inactivity, to control cloud cost.

flisk.reason: A licensed Flisk extra stops idle services with Sablier, which saves local resources, but there is no schedule-based start and stop.

rows.name: Multi-user shared workspace
rows.offer: Several users or groups can connect to one workspace for pairing, on-call or handing over an agent's work for review.

flisk.reason: Sharing needs a remote machine and accounts; a Flisk stack stays on one developer's computer.

rows.name: Read-only sharing of agent chats
rows.offer: A chat can be shared with users or groups who then view messages and stream live updates in read-only mode.

flisk.reason: Flisk has no hosted agent conversations to share between accounts.

rows.name: Port forwarding to workspace services
rows.offer: Developers reach processes in a remote workspace from their own machine through several forwarding methods, including shareable ports.

flisk.reason: Flisk routes each service at a local .localhost address and can open it, but it has no remote forwarding or shareable URL.

rows.name: Ordered startup with dependencies
rows.offer: Startup scripts declare what they depend on so they run in the right order without races, while independent ones run in parallel.

rows.name: Memory and disk alerts
rows.offer: A template block watches the workspace for out-of-memory and out-of-disk conditions and alerts the user.

flisk.reason: flisk doctor checks free disk space, but nothing reports a container killed for running out of memory.

rows.name: Store and inject user secrets
rows.offer: Users store named secrets once and Coder injects them into their workspaces as environment variables or files.

flisk.reason: Flisk generates secrets into an ignored .env and can read them from Infisical, but has no per-user secret store injecting files.

rows.name: Browser terminal into the workspace
rows.offer: A web terminal in the dashboard gives shell access to a workspace with no local setup.

flisk.reason: The services run on the developer's own machine, where a local shell is already available.
